result.title: Understanding Hidden Spatial Preferences in Bayesian Optimization
result.summary: Bayesian optimization uses posterior uncertainty to decide where to explore, but this uncertainty is not spatially neutral. On bounded domains, Gaussian-process posterior variance is typically larger near faces, edges, and corners, giving variance-based acquisition functions a systematic boundary bias. This spatial preference is usually inherited from the surrogate rather than chosen as part of the exploration strategy. We separate these roles by keeping the predictive model fixed and modifying the spatial preference of the exploration term. We control the preference with spatial weight fields and amortize their construction with neural surrogates. Controlled experiments show that the Gaussian process' default boundary bias changes which parts of the domain are explored and which optima are reached. We compare three alternative exploration principles and find, across standard benchmark functions and stochastic robot-pushing tasks, that they can often lower regret, particularly early in the optimization. The spatial structure of posterior uncertainty is therefore not a neutral default: it shapes the exploration strategy and can materially affect optimization performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究贝叶斯优化中高斯过程后验方差在边界、棱角处的系统性偏置如何影响探索，通过空间权重场解耦预测模型与探索项的偏好，并借助神经代理摊销其构造，在基准函数和机器人推物任务上比较三种探索原则。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不确定性并非空间中性、会隐式决定探索位置」的论点，可能为 LVR 中 LOOK/证据获取的偏好偏置与动态计算分配提供类比线索，但领域相隔较远，需人工核查迁移价值。
